problem: λ = 0.10 sits exactly on the lower edge of the stated band and below the friction peak, so calling the action 'hold' is borderline. Below the peak the wheel is under-braked, and a real ABS controller would normally keep building (or hold only briefly) to push slip up toward 0.15. As written, a student may learn that a wheel below the peak should be held.
fix: Say: 'λ = 0.10 is just inside the band at its lower edge, below the 0.15 peak, so ABS would build a little more pressure (or hold briefly) to move slip toward 0.15.' Keep part (b) as it is.

problem: 'The wheel's contact patch tries to move at ωr' is loose and can mislead: in free rolling the contact patch is instantaneously at rest on the road. What is meant is the tread surface speed relative to the axle.
fix: Write: 'The tread surface moves relative to the axle at speed ωr. In free rolling the contact patch is at rest on the road, so ωr = v and the slip velocity v − ωr is zero.'
